newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovakofarma deal boosts SAX index in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Slovakofarma deal boosts SAX index in dull trade.

text.p: A single trade in Slovak pharmaceuticals maker Slovakofarma boosted the Bratislava Stock Exchange's (BSE) SAX index on Monday, though dealers said activity overall was sluggish.
The Slovakofarma trade of around 1,000 shares boosted the issue 119 crowns to 4,414, helping nudge the SAX index up 0.63 points to 177.67.
"At the moment we are in a wait-and-see situation," said Dusan Sykora of ING Barings.
"I would say this is due to the central bank's determination to maintain the crown's current strength and the fact that many don't believe it can and anticipate devaluation," he added.
Sykora said the market was currently under selling pressure with foreign investors staying away, fearing devaluation and falling prices.
Steel maker VSZ gained one crown to 621 on a one small deal, while oil refiner Slovnaft closed unchanged at 850.
Overall volume -- boosted mainly by direct and block trades -- rose to 580,342 shares from 223,231 on Friday and overall turnover was 178.05 million, compared to 105.25 million.
